Bxg2 Rg8 28. Bc6 bxa4 29. Bxa4 Rg1+ 30. Ke2 Rh1. White gains 5 points of material and ends level on material (White has 2 Bishops and 3 Pawns, Black has a Rook and 4 Pawns, 9 points each). The alternative 27. Bxa8 Rg8 28. Bc6 bxa4 29. Bc3+ Ke7 30. h5 Rg5 (136cp) wins 4 points, but Black ends 1 point ahead. A third try, 27. Bc3+ Ke6 28. Bxa8 Rg8 29. Bf3 Rb8 30. axb5 axb5 (120cp), also wins 5 points and ends level. Taking the rook on g2 with 27. Bxg2 is the engine's first choice. All three lines are tactical, and Black's replies in them are not shown as forced.

Position: Right now Black is ahead on the static factors. Black has two Rooks and 5 Pawns (15 points) against White's two Bishops and 4 Pawns (10 points), so Black is 5 points ahead before the tactic. The factors favouring Black are pawn structure (0.16, mostly from White's isolated f2 and h4 pawns), bishops (0.33, with White at -0.33), mobility (0.33) and king safety (0.20, with White at -0.32). These scores are static and do not account for the rook fork. In the top line, king safety moves 0.33 towards White, pawn structure 0.27 and mobility 0.20, so winning the rook also improves White's position. A club-strength player would see the position as roughly balanced.

Tactics:
Nothing is forcing right now: neither side has a piece attacking anything, and no piece is pinned. White is a pawn down after 4...exf4, and the pawn on f4 is what White wants back. The two lines that go for it show how the pawn gets lost again.

The engine's line 5. d4 cxd4 6. Nd5 Bd6 7. Bc4 b5 8. Bb3 Nf6 is tactical. Black takes a pawn on d4 and ends 2 points ahead. The line 5. Nd5 Nf6 6. d4 cxd4 7. Bc4 Bd6 8. O-O O-O is tactical for the same reason: Black ends 2 points ahead. In both lines Black answers d4 with ...cxd4, taking a White pawn, and White does not win a pawn back, so the push loses a pawn. Both of those moves score slightly worse than 5. Bc4 for that reason.

Position:
Stockfish gives White +40cp, which is an equal position with a normal opening edge. A club player would clearly prefer White. Every factor in the list is about even.

- Black's doubled f-pawns (f7, f4) are the main structural feature, but pawn structure is scored about even (White +0.11, Black +0.10).
- King safety is about even (White +0.38, Black +0.40).
- Space is about even (White +0.22, Black +0.32).
- Bishops are about even (both -0.11), and so are rooks (both -0.17).
- Development is slightly ahead for White: the knights on c3 and f3 are out, while Black has only the knight on c6 developed.

The engine's first choice, 5. Bc4, is a quiet move, and its line is positional: 5. Bc4 h6 6. d4 cxd4 7. Nd5 Bc5 8. Bxf4 d6. No material is won, and Black is still 1 point ahead at the end. What the line changes is king safety, which moves 0.36 towards Black. The engine ranks it first because the d4 and Nd5 lines each lose 1 point of material for White. Bc4 is the only one of the three that does not drop a pawn. It also develops the bishop on f1, which is still on its starting square, and the bishop on c4 attacks the pawn on f7.
